body.p: The listing of claims will replace all prior versions, and listings, of claims in the application:

br.br:
1-10. (Canceled)29
11. (Currently Amended) A smart garment for detecting physiological data of a user, the smart garment comprising:a garment configured to be worn on an upper body of the user,
a plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes, wherein each of the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes comprises interlaced conductive fibers for conducting a plurality of ECG signals with respect to the upper body of the user while in contact with skin of the user;
wherein the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes includes at least one textile-based ECG generator electrode for transmitting a generated signal through the patient's user's skinupper body, and at least one textile-based ECG receiver electrode, spaced apart from the textile-based ECG generator electrode, for sensing the generated signal through the user's skin,
a controller device electronically coupled to the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes, the controller device configured to:
generate the generated signal,
transmit the generated signal through the at least one textile-based ECG generator electrode,
sense a collected signal from the at least one textile-based ECG generator electrode via the one or more textile-based ECG receiver ECG electrodes,
based on the collected signal, determine at least one of the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes (i) is at least partially out of contact with the skin of the user and/or (ii) causes the generated signal that is transmitted through the at least one of the textile-based ECG generator electrode to be of unacceptable signal quality,
deselect the at least one determined textile-based ECG electrode, and select at least another one of the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes, and
repeat said generate and said sense of the generated signal using the at least another one of the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes.
12. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 11, wherein the controller determines a percentage of contact surface area of one or more of the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes with the skin of the user.
13. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 11, wherein the controller detects whether one or more of the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes are in acceptable contact with the skin of the user.
14. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 11, further comprising monitoring a signal quality of the generated signal and repeating the process of deselecting the determined textile-based ECG electrode and selecting a different textile-based ECG electrode as a result of said monitoring.
15. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 11, wherein the interlaced conductive fibers comprise conductive yarns.
16. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 15, wherein the conductive yarns are knitted into the ECG electrode.
17. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 11, wherein the controller determines a change in a desired location of one or more of the plurality of the textile-based ECG electrodes.
18. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 11, further comprising a plurality of the ECG generator electrodes and plurality of the ECG receiver electrodes.
19. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 18, wherein the generated signal is generated using a given generator electrode of the plurality of textile-based ECG generator electrodes and the collected signal is sensed using a given receiver electrode of the plurality of textile-based ECG receiver electrodes.
20. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 19, wherein the controller is configured to determine whether the generated signal generated using the given generator electrode and the collected signal sensed using the given receiver electrode does not satisfy a quality threshold, and selects an alternative generator electrode and/or an alternative receiver electrode.
21. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 20, wherein the controller continues selecting alternative generator electrodes and/or alternative receiver electrodes to choose a generator electrode and receiver electrode pairing that satisfies a signal quality threshold.
22. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 11, wherein the garment includes a belt portion having at least one of the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes.
23. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 11, wherein the interlaced conductive fibers are formed by weaving electrically conductive threads.
24. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 11, wherein the controller uses physiological data sensed by the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes to determine a quantity of the user selected from the group consisting of: a PR interval, a QT interval, a corrected QT (QTc) interval, a PR axis, and a QRS axis.
25. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 11, wherein the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes are exposed on a first side and insulated on a second side.
26. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 11, wherein the interlaced conductive fibers are interlaced with non-conductive fibers of a body of the smart garment.
27. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 11, further comprising a conductive trace connected to the each of the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes, each of the conductive traces for connecting the plurality textile-based ECG electrodes to the controller for sending and receiving one or more electronic signals using the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes.
28. (Previously Presented) The smart garment of claim 27, wherein the controller alternates different pairings chosen from the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes as one or more selected pairs in order to determine a decided optimum signal from the one or more electronic signals received from the different pairings.
29. (Currently Amended) A smart garment for detecting physiological data of a user, the smart garment comprising:a plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes, wherein each of the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes comprises interlaced conductive fibers for conducting a plurality of ECG signals with respect to a body of the user;
wherein the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes includes at least one textile-based ECG generator electrode for transmitting a generated signal through the patient's user's bodyskin, and at least one textile-based ECG receiver electrode spaced apart from the textile-based ECG generator electrode for sensing the generated signal through the user's skin,
a controller device electronically coupled to the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes, the controller device configured to:
generate the generated signal,
transmit the generated signal through the at least one textile-based ECG generator electrode,
sense a collected signal via one or more textile-based ECG receiver ECG electrodes,
based on the collected signal, determine at least one of the plurality of textile- based ECG electrodes (i) is at least partially out of contact with skin of the user and/or (ii) causes the generated signal that is transmitted through the at least one ECG generator electrode to be of unacceptable signal quality,
deselect the at least one determined textile-based ECG electrode, and select at least another one of the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes, and
repeat said generate and said sense of the generated signal using the at least another one of the plurality of textile-based ECG electrodes.
30. (Currently Amended) The smart garment of claim 112wherein the controller device is configured to process the collected signal to analyze the physiological data to determine a defined health event of the user.
